races.name: Book Your Christmas Party Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Holy Joe
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's six-year-old arrives on the back of a win over this exact trip on Good ground and holds a strong prominent style that maps perfectly to this race shape; 37 days between runs is not a concern for this yard and the 2/3 record in similar going makes him the most pace-suited runner in the field.

runners_data.name: L'amalric
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy's five-year-old boasts three runs on Good ground and a win at this trip level, but his natural prominence means he has been pushed back to a midfield mapping in this shape — Sean Bowen will need to make a decision early about whether to force the issue forward, and that tactical dilemma tempers his prospects.

runners_data.name: Dolly Dior
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter for Patrick Neville, Dolly Dior recorded her sole win over 2m4f on Good and sets the entire race tempo here; her [STYLE_FIT] tag reflects that she is mapped as lead when she may not always have enjoyed that luxury, and Danny McMenamin must ensure she doesn't go too fast with only four rivals.

runners_data.name: Moi Mon Vieux
runners_data.note: A lightly raced four-year-old with an uncertain tactical style (style=U) and a headgear flag to note — only one run on Good ground from two career starts — meaning Richard Hobson's runner carries the most unknowns of anything in this field and his chance is hard to quantify with confidence.

runners_data.name: Fortunes Dawn
runners_data.note: Derek Fox partners this seven-year-old for William Young Jnr, but back-to-back defeats over 2m4f and 2m6f on Good ground (finishing 9th and 7th respectively) and a 0W0P record in similar conditions paint a bleak picture; the hold-up style requires a truly run race that this shape is unlikely to provide.

races.paceDynamic: Dolly Dior is the confirmed front-runner here and, in a field of just five, should be able to dictate an unchallenged, measured gallop from the outset on Good ground over 2m4f at Perth. Holy Joe and L'amalric are both naturally prominent types, though L'amalric has been redistributed to a midfield mapping because there is simply not enough room at the head of affairs for all three — in practice, Holy Joe is the most likely to secure a prominent berth directly behind Dolly Dior, while L'amalric may be shuffled back against his nature. Fortunes Dawn is a genuine hold-up horse and Moi Mon Vieux, whose style is uncertain, adds a minor unknown quantity but is unlikely to disrupt the tempo. With Dolly Dior controlling an uncontested, sustainable pace and the field compact, this race shape strongly favours a prominent-racing, travelling horse who can sit just off the leader and pounce at the second-last — making Holy Joe's profile the most tactically advantaged.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dolly Dior Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Dolly Dior bowls along in front at a controlled, honest gallop and the small field strings out behind without pressure.
scenarios.body: Dolly Dior sets a rhythm that suits herself through the staying trip, and a horse tracking her closely throughout — particularly Holy Joe — gets first run two out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Holy Joe travels fluently just off Dolly Dior and produces a clean jump two out to assert.
scenarios.body: The race turns into a two-horse contest from the home turn, with Holy Joe's Good-ground form (2-1 in similar conditions) giving him the decisive edge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Gets Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to compromise the leaders and Fortunes Dawn or Moi Mon Vieux produce a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Fortunes Dawn has failed to fire recently in similar conditions but a stop-start jumps race could create gaps to exploit; Moi Mon Vieux's unknown style is the wildcard here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Disrupted Pace Scrambles Field
scenarios.trigger: If L'amalric pushes forward from his mapped midfield position and creates unexpected pressure on Dolly Dior early.
scenarios.body: A contested pace over this trip on Good ground would compress the race and open the door for the freshest jumper, but this scenario relies on L'amalric racing well out of his redistributed role, making it the least likely shape.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether L'amalric's connections allow him to drift back quietly or whether Sean Bowen pushes forward to challenge Dolly Dior — if L'amalric goes prominent, the pace dynamic changes entirely and could unsettle Dolly Dior's rhythm.

Moi Mon Vieux's unknown style (style=U) and headgear flag mean his early positioning is unpredictable — if he jumps well and finds a prominent spot, he becomes a more dangerous unknown quantity than his odds may suggest.

Fortunes Dawn's hold-up profile is a structural mismatch with a small, slowly run field at Perth — watch for Derek Fox positioning him closer than expected early, as his two recent Good-ground reverses suggest he needs an unusual race shape to get involved.

Holy Joe's jumping record should be monitored — a last-time-out win over this trip included a fall entry in recent form (U in prior), and clean jumping at the critical second-last hurdle will be essential if he is to convert a prominent position into a victory.

races.name: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Ras Kassar
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old with progressive form (two wins in last five), handled at handicap level in France before switching yards; comes in fresh at 42 days off, hold-up style sits against him in a slow-tempo race, and the step down to 2m from his recent 2m4f trips on the all-weather may slightly suit a sharper surface, but he needs genuine pace to close into.

runners_data.name: Conquer The Breeze
runners_data.note: Pace-setter in a field where no one is likely to challenge him for the lead; excellent Perth course form (2W from 2 on Good), Ryan Mania maintains continuity in the saddle, and trainer Adam Nicol has one winner from five runners in the past 14 days; the rare risk is he has raced prominently rather than solo-from-front before, but conditions are near-perfect for him today.

runners_data.name: Hypotenus
runners_data.note: Richie McLernon partners a horse who is admirably consistent but yet to win in his last 15 outings; form figures of 3-3-3-4-6 around 2m on Good or soft underline his reliability without asserting a winning claim, and the steady pace set by Conquer The Breeze is unlikely to create the gaps needed for a horse of his profile.

runners_data.name: Tree Top Tyson
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes links up with a horse returning from 171 days off — the fitness query is real — but when fresh he has won and placed, and his prominent style ideally positions him to shadow Conquer The Breeze throughout; the significant absence means condition on the day is the primary concern, and Patrick Neville has no recent runners on record to gauge stable form.

runners_data.name: Garde Des Champs
runners_data.note: Lucinda Russell and Michael Scudamore's consistent ten-year-old has strong Good-ground credentials (13 of 15 sim-going runs showing), but his natural style is to race from the rear and he will be working against the grain in a race the pace map places him in midfield; Alan Doyle's 3lb claim helps the handicap weight, though the style mismatch tempers expectations significantly.

runners_data.name: Kinbara Firstdraft
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by inclination, Conor Rabbitt's 3lb claim softens the burden from 156lbs, but form figures of 4-7-5-4-7 tell a story of a horse that rarely threatens the winner; racing into a position more forward than is natural for him, and with only two wins from 15 similar-going runs, the scenario in which he features prominently at the finish is the least likely in this field.

races.paceDynamic: Conquer The Breeze is the sole confirmed front runner in a six-runner field and, with no rival likely to genuinely challenge for the lead from flag fall, Ryan Mania can dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop over the 2m Perth circuit on Good ground. Tree Top Tyson has prominent tendencies and may track closely, but the pace is unlikely to be pressured into something genuinely punishing, creating a steady rhythm that suits those in touch rather than those coming from off it. The field actually contains more hold-up types than can all settle at the rear in their natural position — Garde Des Champs and Kinbara Firstdraft are genuine hold-up performers pushed into a mapped midfield slot, meaning their true late-run threat is constrained by a shape that will not generate the strong pace they need to close into. This race shape — an uncontested front runner setting an honest but manageable tempo — most clearly favours horses racing prominently or able to track the leader through the race, giving them first run from the second-last fence onwards.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Conquer The Breeze Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Conquer The Breeze is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and sets a controlled but honest tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Ryan Mania rolls the field along at a metronomic gallop, kicking from the front at the second-last and exploiting his Good-ground course form (2W from 2 at Perth on similar ground); with no genuine pace pressurer to exhaust him early, he is hardest to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight Out
scenarios.trigger: If Tree Top Tyson tracks Conquer The Breeze aggressively and both fight out a two-horse duel to the line.
scenarios.body: Brian Hughes pushes Tree Top Tyson into the slip-stream early and the pair gradually pull clear of the hold-up horses who cannot generate enough closing pace on the steady tempo; Tree Top Tyson's win at this trip and course-similar Good ground gives him the profile to prevail if Conquer The Breeze ties up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace genuinely quickens mid-race and creates enough of a test that one of the closers can sustain a run from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Ras Kassar, the most unexposed of the hold-up types at just five years old and in career-best form (two recent wins), would be best placed to pick up late if the tempo genuinely rises; Hypotenus has consistent form around this trip and going but needs a stronger pace than is likely to materialise here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Veteran Garde Des Champs Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If significant errors at fences disrupt the front pair and open the race up for a flat-out finish.
scenarios.body: Garde Des Champs carries ten-year-old legs but is consistent on Good ground with 13 of 15 similar-going runs in the frame; a strongly run final quarter-mile would be needed to bring him fully into play, but his redistribution from hold-up to midfield makes the scenario largely dependent on race chaos.

watchPoints.text: Conquer The Breeze — watch whether Ryan Mania is pressed at any point in the first half-mile; if Tree Top Tyson sits tight on his quarters, the dynamic shifts from controlled dictation to a potential pace battle that could open the race for the closers.

Tree Top Tyson — 171 days off the track is a significant layoff for a jumper; watch the paddock for any sign of a horse that is burly or not tuned for peak effort, as fitness level here is the single biggest variable in the race.

Garde Des Champs — given only 10 days since his last run (quick turnaround), monitor his jumping for any signs of tiredness in the closing stages; he is at the end of a busy spell and Alan Doyle will need a clean round to have any chance of landing a late blow.

Ras Kassar — watch early to see where Rian Corcoran (5lb claim) actually positions him; if the pace is slower than expected and Corcoran is forced to commit earlier than ideal, his hold-up profile is wasted and his chance all but gone.

Kinbara Firstdraft — observe whether Conor Rabbitt attempts to gain a forward position from the gate; if he does, it signals Kerr's camp has changed tactics, which would be the only meaningful scenario in which this horse features late.

races.name: Saints In The Community Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Noble Birth
runners_data.note: Has clearly taken the lead role here; nine-year-old with acceptable Good-ground form at 2m4f but a 79-day absence and a form string that includes a pull-up is a concern — Charlie Maggs's 3lb claim helps the weight but this horse is racing out of its usual prominent-tracking role by actually leading.

runners_data.name: Bold Light
runners_data.note: Trainer Russell/Scudamore yard in fair 14-day form (2/17); prominent racer whose sole similar-going placing was distant and form on Good ground thin — headgear (p) noted but the step up to 2m4f on Good may not fully suit a horse whose best efforts came on Soft.

runners_data.name: Atlantic City
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen is a major booking for Olly Murphy's five-year-old; seven of twelve runs on Good or similar, one win and six places, and recent form shows a win and a second at 2m on Good — prominent style sits perfectly in the map's dominant scenario and the trip looks within range.

runners_data.name: Lets Mingle
runners_data.note: Described as an unknown style, which adds uncertainty to placement; back in 29 days with a recent fifth at this trip and a third at 2m on Good — Jack Power's 5lb claim is useful and a horse that can adapt tactically carries a small edge if the race shape shifts.

runners_data.name: Summergrounds
runners_data.note: Nicky Richards' ten-year-old was out just 16 days ago, finishing third, showing freshness; consistent prominent racer with eight placings on similar ground and a win from 15 runs, and the 2m4f Good surface is well within range — age is the only nagging doubt.

runners_data.name: Ceol Draiochta
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up type from Adam Nicol's yard, 49 days since last run; all recent form at shorter trips (16f) so stepping up to 2m4f is a notable query — seven of nine runs on Good-type ground but a form string of F0/P-4 is modest at best.

runners_data.name: Pure Gold
runners_data.note: Lisa Harrison's six-year-old has been in action just 10 days ago; naturally a prominent racer — the crowded pace picture means it is likely to be shuffled further back than it would prefer, and a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.90 tempers confidence in it delivering from an unnatural position despite solid recent consistency.

runners_data.name: Parikarma
runners_data.note: Miss Imogen Mathias (7lb claimer) rides the nine-year-old who wears a hood; hold-up type with two runs at 2m4f on Good in recent history both yielding a place — Samuel Drinkwater's 0/2 in the last 14 days is modest but the trip and ground combination here is probably the best fit in the field for this horse.

runners_data.name: Struth
runners_data.note: Wears tongue-strap and a hood; hold-up type whose last six runs have all been placed fifth, sixth or worse — Lucinda Russell/Michael Scudamore team have him fit enough (35 days) but a string of 055-66 and ten of fifteen runs on Good-type ground producing zero wins points to a horse that finds ways to finish midpack rather than challenge.

races.paceDynamic: Noble Birth is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, is set to control from the front at a sustainable, unchallenged gallop over this 2m4f trip on Good ground at Perth. Atlantic City, Bold Light, and Summergrounds are all prominent types who will push to track closely, creating a compact early order but not a truly pressured pace — Noble Birth dictates the terms. Pure Gold is a natural prominent runner redistributed to midfield on the map because the three horses above are better placed to secure those positions, meaning Pure Gold is likely to find itself racing further back than ideal. This race shape — a lone leader setting an honest but manageable tempo over a strongly run 2m4f — strongly favours prominent-to-mid-pack closers who travel economically and have the stamina to grind out the final climb, rather than either true front-runners or deep hold-up horses who need a truly searching pace to reel them in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Noble Birth controls at a comfortable clip and the prominent trio race in his slipstream before striking turning in.
scenarios.body: Noble Birth bowls along unchallenged and the race becomes a test of who travels best in behind, with the winner coming from those positioned just off the pace with cover; Atlantic City, with the best recent Good-ground form and Sean Bowen aboard, and Summergrounds, placed repeatedly at this trip, are ideally suited to land the spoils from this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so gentle that Noble Birth steals enough of a margin turning in that hold-up horses can never close.
scenarios.body: Noble Birth, racing out of role by leading but clearly comfortable doing so here, builds on a soft gallop and the field never quickens sufficiently to reel him in; his Good-ground form at this trip is acceptable and a 9lb claimer saving weight helps.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race and the closers get a genuine sprint finish off a slow tempo.
scenarios.body: Parikarma and Ceol Draiochta, operating from the back, would benefit if the race becomes an attritional test where stamina and a late run matter most; Parikarma's best form comes at 2m4f on Good ground and a slow pace suits her profile most.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent horses contest the early lead aggressively, burning the field out and leaving the race open to anything.
scenarios.body: Should Bold Light or Summergrounds challenge Noble Birth early and force a contested gallop, fatigue sets in and the race fragments; Lets Mingle, versatile in style, and Parikarma from further back could capitalise on a field that has overcooked the pace.

watchPoints.text: Atlantic City's booking of Sean Bowen in a race with one confirmed front-runner and a pace shape that suits prominent closers is the single biggest flag — watch whether he slots just behind Noble Birth from the off.

Pure Gold has raced just 10 days ago and is a natural front-runner likely to find itself racing in mid-division against its instincts — monitor in the betting for any drift that reflects punters recognising this mismatch.

Noble Birth's 79-day absence combined with a pull-up last time and a nine-year-old profile means any sign of fatigue jumping the final two flights could quickly unwind what looks like a comfortable lead.

Parikarma's amateur rider (7lb claim) saves meaningful weight for a hold-up horse that genuinely stays 2m4f on Good — if the race develops a searching gallop late, the weight advantage becomes significant.

Summergrounds was out only 16 days ago and finished third; a trainer running a horse back quickly at Nicky Richards' level usually signals the horse is fit and the race conditions are considered ideal — proximity at the weights is worth noting.

races.name: Sport, Education & Wellbeing Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Statuario
runners_data.note: Three wins at the 2m4f–3m range on Good ground give Sean Bowen's mount strong trip and going credentials, and the 35-day break looks sharp enough; a pure hold-up operator who needs the pace to be honest enough to make his late challenge count — may find this controlled tempo insufficient.

runners_data.name: Parisencore
runners_data.note: Nicky Richards' front-runner sets the table for the entire race and on Good ground has a 10/15 similarity hit; carries a [STYLE_FIT] flag suggesting this is not his ideal role, but with no other confirmed pace-maker he will almost certainly lead — the question is whether he has enough left over the final 3m.

runners_data.name: Bleu D'enfer
runners_data.note: Theo Gillard takes the ride on a horse fitted with a tongue-tie and pad headgear combination, fresh off a 58-day break that may have sharpened him; only 7/15 on similar-going profile is a mild flag, and he is a hold-up type who will need to find improvement over this 3m trip on Good ground.

runners_data.name: Grand Clermont
runners_data.note: Rian Corcoran (5lb claim) partners David Pipe's consistent horse back at a 3m trip after recent placing form over shorter; good-ground form is solid (4/15 sim-going) and a tongue-tie-wearing prominent racer who can sit just off Parisencore makes this a natural fit for the dominant scenario.

runners_data.name: Walk On Quest
runners_data.note: Lucinda Russell and Michael Scudamore's seven-year-old was placed over 3m on Good at Perth recently and returns 35 days later with a tongue-tie; a prominent runner by style who is likely to lock into the tracking position just behind Parisencore — Derek Fox will be looking to produce him from a ground-saving position.

runners_data.name: Wasdell Dundalk
runners_data.note: Callum Bewley rides a horse whose natural racing style is off the pace, but the excess of rear-facing types in this field means he is unlikely to get a true hold-up run; his 9/15 Good-going record is the best in the race on that metric, but OR 112 and a [STYLE_FIT] concern limit confidence unless the pace genuinely tests the leaders.

runners_data.name: Inis Oirr
runners_data.note: Patrick Wadge's mount boasts solid recent form including wins and places over 3m on Good ground, and the 35-day freshener suits; a genuine hold-up performer who will struggle to settle as far back as he ideally wants given others in the field are also seeking rear positions — headgear (blinkers) may keep him more focussed but the positional compromise is real.

races.paceDynamic: Parisencore is the single confirmed front-runner here and, with no other genuine pace-maker to press them, Danny McMenamin can dictate a controlled, honest gallop over the 3m trip on Good ground — sustainable rather than searching, which keeps the race together for longer than a truly contested pace scenario would. Grand Clermont and Walk On Quest are genuine prominent types who will look to track close to Parisencore, creating a compact lead group of three across the first circuit before the race begins to stretch out on the final loop. Behind them, Statuario, Bleu D'enfer, Wasdell Dundalk and Inis Oirr occupy the chasing pack, though it should be noted that Wasdell Dundalk and Inis Oirr are genuine hold-up operators who have been pushed forward on the map because the field holds more rear-facing types than can all naturally sit at the back — in reality they may find themselves closer than ideal, competing with each other for cover. With one honest pace-setter setting a measured tempo and no pressure to quicken early, this race shape most favours prominent closers who can travel fluidly in behind the leader and pick up efficiently from two out — horses with proven Good-ground form over this trip who do not need a strongly-run race to find their best.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Parisencore Controls, Prominent Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Parisencore dictates an uncontested, moderate pace and the race is decided by who can pick up most cleanly from two fences out.
scenarios.body: Parisencore bowls along comfortably in front with Grand Clermont and Walk On Quest tracking in a tight pocket, and the decisive move comes from one of those prominent stalkers as the field straightens for home; horses who travel well with cover and jump fluently at pace are rewarded by this shape. Statuario's hold-up style may leave him needing a stronger pace to get competitive, while Bleu D'enfer could creep into contention from the rear if jumping holds together.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Statuario Picks Them Off Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally stronger than expected in the closing mile, creating enough of a tempo for a hold-up finisher to close powerfully.
scenarios.body: Sean Bowen bides his time aboard Statuario before producing a sustained run from the home turn, as a compressed field and a genuine gallop suits his patient style and 11yo course-track profile; his 11/15 Good-going record and three winning performances at this trip underline his credentials when pace does his work.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Parisencore Front-Runs And Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Parisencore jumps particularly fluently and builds enough of an advantage that the prominent rivals can never quite get to grips.
scenarios.body: Richards' runner, already rated a [STYLE_FIT] concern for this position, confounds expectations by making every yard at a rhythm that suits only a clean jumper leading from pillar to post; the prominent chasers find Parisencore has stolen sufficient margins at the fences to hold on into the run-in.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that Wasdell Dundalk or Inis Oirr, despite being redistributed from their natural rear positions, are able to close from off the pace.
scenarios.body: This is a lower-probability outcome because both Wasdell Dundalk and Inis Oirr carry [REDISTRIBUTED] and [STYLE_FIT] flags, meaning they are unlikely to access their true hold-up role in this shape; only a notably stronger gallop than Parisencore's typical front-running tempo would create enough space for them to deliver a sustained late run.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Grand Clermont or Walk On Quest immediately press Parisencore from the first fence — if both sit within a length of the leader, the front of the race becomes very competitive and the tempo could quicken sharply, changing the entire pace dynamic.

Wasdell Dundalk and Inis Oirr are both natural hold-up horses competing for rear positions — if they crowd each other in the early stages and neither settles cleanly, one or both could be forced to race prominently in an unnatural role, risking a stamina failure late over 3m.

Bleu D'enfer's 58-day layoff at age 8 with headgear fitted is worth monitoring at the fences — a jumping error or loss of momentum from ring-rustiness could compromise his ability to make ground from off the pace on a track that rewards fluent jumpers.

Statuario's jockey Sean Bowen rode the horse to a recent Perth win over 2m4f on Good — if Bowen angles for an outside run rather than getting blocked in the rear group, watch for him to begin his move earlier than expected approaching the third-last.

races.name: Saints Kidz Community Football Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Ballintubber Boy
runners_data.note: Hold-up style that suits a sole front-runner scenario perfectly; Toby McCain-Mitchell (3lb claimer) takes off useful weight, and sim-going record of 2W7P from 15 runs on Good gives strong confidence at this venue and conditions; 31 days since last run is no concern given trainer form.

runners_data.name: Secret Trix
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen is a major booking for Olly Murphy (5 winners from 14 in last 14 days), and this hold-up type has placed on Good ground on multiple occasions over this sort of trip; headgear (tp) is a constant, going record is solid, and the 38-day break is well within normal bounds.

runners_data.name: Speed Davis
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner with a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93, meaning his chance should be tempered — he is fundamentally a prominent racer but is mapped leading here; sim-going figures of only 8 from 15 are modest, and Donald McCain has 0 from 14 in the past 14 days, though his lead role is not in doubt if he jumps cleanly.

runners_data.name: Spit Spot
runners_data.note: Lucinda Russell and Michael Scudamore's 7yo has a prominent style but has been off 81 days (37 days with a flag), raising fitness questions; the best Perth form in his record comes over shorter trips, and his recent form string of 1647P is inconsistent — the fitness query is the dominant concern.

runners_data.name: Lowlands
runners_data.note: Nicky Richards' 7yo is a genuine hold-up horse by trade, but with multiple true closers in this field, he has been mapped to midfield on the chart — that positional compromise may cost him the clean passage he needs; his form (223-12) and sim-going record are strong, and Danny McMenamin should manage him sensibly, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) reflects the crowded rear.

runners_data.name: Ebselysees
runners_data.note: Two recent wins at this sort of distance (24f and 26f) make Ebselysees lively on form, but like Lowlands he is a natural hold-up type squeezed into a midfield slot on this map simply because there are too many true closers; Nathan Moscrop must judge a clever position, and the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) means his chance is structurally discounted in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Dalileo
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes rides a lightly-weighted 11yo for Lisa Harrison (0 from 1 in 14 days) who won 10 days ago on Good — quick turnaround is a minor flag but the horse has obvious recent form; prominent in style, he would benefit most if Speed Davis's gallop becomes genuinely demanding and grinds the hold-up horses out of the contest.

races.paceDynamic: Speed Davis is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to press him, he is set to bowl along in front at a sustainable clip over the 3m trip on Good ground at Perth. Spit Spot and Dalileo add prominent-profile company but neither is a natural pace-setter, so Speed Davis should dictate terms without serious pressure, creating a race run at an honest but manageable tempo — not a lung-busting gallop. This shape — a controlled, uncontested lead — classically favours hold-up horses who can conserve energy and mount a sustained late challenge on the long run-in, making Ballintubber Boy and Secret Trix the profiles most architecturally suited to the finish. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Lowlands and Ebselysees are genuine come-from-behind horses redistributed into midfield on the map because they cannot all realistically slot into their natural rearward berth, meaning those two will need to overcome a positional compromise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Speed Davis sets a measured, uncontested gallop and hold-up horses get the patient run they need.
scenarios.body: Speed Davis rolls along comfortably in front on Good ground, giving the field a rhythmical tempo that suits those held up off the pace; Ballintubber Boy and Secret Trix, both in good form and suited by this trip and going, get the ideal conditions to unleash their finishing effort on the Perth straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Speed Davis Wins Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Speed Davis is allowed to completely dictate and the hold-up horses fail to close the gap on the long run-in.
scenarios.body: Racing off a natural lead with no pressure, Speed Davis could simply steal margins through jumping precision and controlled galloping, arriving at the last with enough in reserve; his recent win form (two wins in last five) at similar trips and going lend credibility to this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Speed Davis goes too hard early or makes a jumping error that fractures the field and opens a gap for the backmarkers.
scenarios.body: A misjudged pace or error by Speed Davis would compress the field and reward horses like Lowlands and Ebselysees who are tracking further back — though both are mapped forward of their true position, a genuine collapse of pace could still bring them into play.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves deceptively strong and mid-race pressure grinds down the hold-up horses before they can produce their finish.
scenarios.body: Spit Spot or Dalileo, travelling up with the pace, could benefit if the hold-up brigade are caught flat-footed or the race becomes a war of attrition in a strong gallop; Dalileo's recent win on Good and Brian Hughes's positional nous are relevant if this scenario materialises.

watchPoints.text: Speed Davis's jumping is pivotal — if he makes an error at an early flight, the field will close and the redistribution problem for Lowlands and Ebselysees becomes relevant immediately.
Spit Spot's fitness after 81 days off is unproven; if he fades from a prominent position on the second circuit, he could cause interference in a compact field over 3m at Perth.

Lowlands and Ebselysees, both true hold-up horses mapped to midfield, will be watching for a gap that may not open in a smoothly-run race — Danny McMenamin and Nathan Moscrop need to react quickly if the race bunches at the top of the straight.
Dalileo ran only 10 days ago — monitor in-running behaviour for signs of staleness, particularly if he is pushed forward by Brian Hughes to track the pace sooner than expected.
Ballintubber Boy and Secret Trix are both on 168lbs and hold the highest OR in the field; if either is burdened in a stop-start pace, the weight could blunt their finishing kick on the Perth run-in.

races.name: Scone Palace International Horse Trials Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Centurion's Sister
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter with a clean prominent profile; handles Good ground well (four recent runs on similar) but no wins in nine similar-going starts — a front-runner who has placed often without winning off OR 100, so durability of her lead is the key question.

runners_data.name: Scots Poet
runners_data.note: Excellent course-and-distance record with three wins from 15 Good-ground starts and a 2/16f/GOO at the top of her recent form string; Ewan Whillans yard has one winner from nine in the past fortnight so form is quiet but Scots Poet's own profile here is strong.

runners_data.name: Follow Charlie
runners_data.note: Hold-up type fitted with a hood who has been running over longer trips (20-24f) recently and now drops back to 2m; Mike Smith's yard has no runners in the past 14 days and 59 days off, so freshness is an unknown — the hood and shorter trip could sharpen him up.

runners_data.name: Jolyjump
runners_data.note: 378 days off the track is a significant flag for a six-year-old, though his form before the layoff included a 2/16f/GOO and 2/17f/GOO showing he handles this trip and ground — Gary & Josh Moore's yard has been active (4/26) so he arrives fit if not match-sharp.

runners_data.name: Tigress Lilly
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up specialist with a string of mid-to-rear finishes (6-11th range) on Good ground; despite being mapped to midfield to reflect the field's hold-up bias, she has never placed on Good going across five attempts and the style-fit concern applies.

runners_data.name: Storm The Dug
runners_data.note: True rear-of-field type whose best effort was a 2/16f/GOO from off the pace last time; shown in midfield here because of the redistribution — his Cheltenham-level stable form (1/13 in 14 days) is modest and he has zero wins from 12 Good-ground starts.

runners_data.name: Malangen
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old with genuine Good-ground affinity (11 runs, four places including back-to-back 2nd finishes at 16f and 20f on Good); Lisa Harrison's yard sends just one runner in 14 days and he is 10 days fresh — veteran but consistent enough to be a player racing prominently.

runners_data.name: Lucky In Taipan
runners_data.note: 300 days off the track is the standout concern; a natural hold-up type mapped to midfield who has never won and has only one place from seven Good-ground starts — Fergal O'Brien's yard won one of eight runners in 14 days but this profile asks a lot on return.

races.paceDynamic: Centurion's Sister is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner 2m hurdle at Perth and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she is likely to dictate an uncontested, measured gallop on Good ground. Scots Poet and Malangen are the natural prominent types who will sit just off the pace, and with Centurion's Sister not being pressured, the tempo is likely to be controlled and sustainable rather than brutal. The three hold-up horses — Tigress Lilly, Storm The Dug, and Lucky In Taipan — have been mapped to midfield because the field holds more true hold-up types than can realistically find their natural rear position in a race this size, meaning their actual tactical influence may differ from their preferred style. A controlled, front-runner-dominated shape strongly favours horses that travel prominently and can quicken from a close-up position off a steady pace — Centurion's Sister, Scots Poet, and Malangen are best positioned to exploit this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Centurion's Sister Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Centurion's Sister leads uncontested and sets a sustainable gallop that rewards prominent racers.
scenarios.body: She bowls along at the head of affairs, dictating a moderate tempo that drains the finishing speed from those held up, and arrives at the last with a decisive advantage over those who couldn't get close enough.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Outstay Her
scenarios.trigger: If Scots Poet or Malangen press Centurion's Sister throughout and grind her down in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: A stronger pace than anticipated develops as the prominent pair refuse to simply follow, turning the race into a stamina test over the final flight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a late run for one of the redistributed hold-up types.
scenarios.body: Storm The Dug or Jolyjump, tracking closer than their natural style suggests, produce a late challenge if the leaders have emptied out by the final hurdle — though the style-fit discounts on Tigress Lilly and Lucky In Taipan reduce confidence in this shape materialising.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Produces Shock Result
scenarios.trigger: If the race unravels through a fall, blunder, or catastrophic misjudgement of pace by the leader.
scenarios.body: Lucky In Taipan or Tigress Lilly, at big prices and racing out of their natural role, could scramble home in a ragged finish — but this scenario requires multiple things to go wrong for the market leaders simultaneously.

watchPoints.text: Centurion's Sister — if she builds a decisive lead approaching the final hurdle unchallenged, she has the fitness (16 days fresh) and course form to hold on; watch whether Scots Poet or Malangen put her under pressure or simply follow.
Jolyjump — 378 days absent means his jumping could be rusty early; a bad mistake or fidgety start from him could disrupt the rhythm of any horses nearby.

Storm The Dug and Tigress Lilly — both are mapped out of their natural hold-up role; watch whether they actually get trapped wide or are forced to race far more prominently than ideal, which could drain their stamina before the final flight.

Lucky In Taipan — 300 days off and a hold-up type racing out of position; monitor in the betting market as any significant move would suggest stable confidence that outweighs the form concerns on return.
